claims.statement: build-win/ is a pre-configured CMake build tree (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Windows, x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix from /home/jambo/buildkit/mingw/root, Ninja, Release); a plain `cmake --build build-win --target TONE3000_Standalone` produces build-win/plugin/TONE3000_artefacts/Release/Standalone/TONE3000.exe, a self-contained PE32+ x86-64 exe whose DLL imports must be Windows API DLLs only (no libstdc++/libgcc/libwinpthread). (test/CMakeLists.txt cited only as the repo's CMakeLists reference; the windows-build rule lives in docs.)

The root CMakeLists.txt carries two idempotent MinGW configure-time patches that ASIO and DirectWrite need under MinGW and must be kept: T3K_MINGW_ASIO_SEH (rewrite the ASIO SDK's C-style __try/__except SEH to if/else in juce_audio_devices/asio/WINASIO.cpp) and T3K_MINGW_DWRITE_CRP (route IDWriteFactory::CreateCustomRenderingParams through the base COM interface in juce_graphics/fonts/juce_DirectWriteTypeface.cpp, whose MinGW header hides it behind the vtable). ASIO is a hard user requirement, ON by default via JUCE's bundled ASIO SDK. MinGW's libstdc++ lacks std::tanhf/std::floorf, so the codebase uses std::tanh/std::floor with float args.

Wine smoke test on WSLg: WINEPREFIX=/home/jambo/wine-test WINEDEBUG=-all DISPLAY=:0 wineboot -u, then timeout --signal=KILL 30 wine64 TONE3000.exe; exit 124 (had to SIGKILL a live app) means success, and an ALSA /dev/snd/seq 'No such file' line is expected with no audio device. Wine has no real ASIO driver, so this proves launch but not the ASIO dropdown; static proof the ASIO type compiled in is strings TONE3000.exe | grep -i ASIOAudioIODevice.

script/win-standalone.sh (the former scripts/win-standalone.sh, folded into script/ by the repo-organization reorg) stages the built TONE3000.exe to C:\Users\jambo\Downloads\TONE3000-win-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (run-timestamp only, never descriptive suffixes; older descriptive folders are historical A/B references to leave alone), with -2/-3 dedup, md5sums, and the git branch + HEAD commit printed for provenance. A plain build does not pick up a changed .env (publishable key) or new sources — it needs a reconfigure (GLOB re-runs) ~2 min.
